newsitem.title: USA: Hartmarx sees improved gross margins.
newsitem.headline: Hartmarx sees improved gross margins.

text.p: Hartmarx Corp said it expects gross margins in its business attire lines to improve "as a more stabilized environment materializes."
In 1996, the textiles concern said tailored clothing sales were strong and "every major men's operating unit and the womens apparel group showed sales increases."

At the end of the year, the company's equity-to-debt ratio was at its highest level since 1991. "Over $90 million of equity has been added since 1992, while debt has been reduced by $146 million," Hartmarx said.

Interest expense declined in 1996 by 16 percent to 2.7 percent of sales. "We intend to maintain our focus on deleveraging, with a long-term objective of lowering interest expense to less than 1.5 percent of sales," Hartmarx said.

The company also said its objective is to reduce operating expenses to less than 20 percent of sales by 1998. "Operating expenses were cut by $5.1 million to 20.9 percent of sales (in 1996) from 22.3 percent of sales in 1995," the company said.
